title: AI Power Index v2.0 Pilot — Evidence-Backed Power Profiles
definition: AI power is an entity's sustained ability to influence access, terms, deployment, or the distribution of value in an AI-relevant market by controlling a consequential dependency that counterparties cannot readily replace or bypass.
aggregation_policy: The pilot does not sum, average, normalize, rank, or convert ordinal judgments into a composite score.
missing_evidence_policy: Missing or ambiguous evidence is unknown. A zero grade requires affirmative evidence and is never inferred from nondisclosure.

force_domains.label: Compute
force_domains.definition: Control over AI production capability, including relevant hardware, manufacturing, models, software ecosystems, or capacity access.

force_domains.label: Interface
force_domains.definition: Control over distribution, customer relationships, defaults, workflows, and routes from AI output to action.

force_domains.label: Alignment — Governance & permission control
force_domains.definition: Authority over consequential AI behavior, access conditions, deployment rules, and adopted standards.

force_domains.label: Energy
force_domains.definition: Control over deliverable electricity and enabling physical infrastructure in the relevant location and timeframe.

criteria.label: Control
criteria.question: What can the entity decide or enforce?

anchors.label: No relevant right
anchors.definition: Affirmative evidence shows no relevant decision right in the scoped mechanism.

anchors.label: Self-use
anchors.definition: Rights principally support the entity's own use; external terms remain controlled elsewhere.

anchors.label: Counterparty leverage
anchors.definition: Documented enforceable rights affect a material counterparty's access, allocation, or terms.

anchors.label: Market-shaping control
anchors.definition: Documented ability to set or enforce consequential terms across multiple material counterparties in the defined market.

criteria.label: Substitution constraint
criteria.question: How difficult is it to replace or bypass this dependency today?

anchors.label: Routine alternatives
anchors.definition: Affirmative evidence shows usable alternatives without material disruption.

anchors.label: Bounded switching
anchors.definition: Alternatives are usable but require bounded integration or switching work.

anchors.label: Material constraint
anchors.definition: Evidence shows material switching cost, qualification delay, capacity limits, or performance loss.

anchors.label: No viable substitute
anchors.definition: Evidence shows no currently viable alternative at the specified requirements and scale.

criteria.label: Realized leverage / value capture
criteria.question: Is the control position producing observable outcomes?

anchors.label: Leverage neutralized
anchors.definition: Affirmative evidence shows counterparties bypass or neutralize the claimed leverage.

anchors.label: Participation only
anchors.definition: Commercial use exists, but reviewed outcomes show only ordinary participation.

anchors.label: Observable leverage
anchors.definition: Favorable terms, retained economics, allocation influence, or customer commitment are documented and linked to the mechanism.

anchors.label: Repeated leverage
anchors.definition: Mechanism-linked outcomes recur across multiple material counterparties or reporting periods.

criteria.label: Durability
criteria.question: What supports persistence over the next 24 months?

anchors.label: Near-term loss
anchors.definition: Documented expiry, displacement, or loss is expected within 12 months.

anchors.label: Bounded continuation
anchors.definition: Evidence supports continuation into 12–24 months, but a known limit bounds it.

anchors.label: 24-month support
anchors.definition: Rights, replacement timelines, or structural barriers support the 24-month thesis, subject to named risks.

anchors.label: Cycle-tested persistence
anchors.definition: The 24-month thesis also has evidence of renewal or persistence across prior commercial or technology cycles.

summary_states.label: Insufficient evidence
summary_states.rule: Control or substitution cannot be graded with at least Moderate confidence.

summary_states.label: Power not established in this mechanism
summary_states.rule: Supported Control or Substitution is below 2.

summary_states.label: Structural potential
summary_states.rule: Control and Substitution are at least 2, but Realized leverage is below 2 or unknown.

summary_states.label: Demonstrated leverage
summary_states.rule: Control, Substitution, and Realized leverage are at least 2 and the mechanism is operational.

summary_states.label: Demonstrated leverage; durability supported
summary_states.rule: Demonstrated leverage plus Durability at least 2.

confidence_policy.high: Appropriate primary evidence directly supports the claim and scope; material comparative assertions are independently or counterparty-corroborated; current validity is checked; no unresolved material contradiction remains.
confidence_policy.moderate: Appropriate primary evidence supports the core fact, while the anchor requires a disclosed bounded inference and no unresolved contradiction changes the grade.
confidence_policy.limited: Promotional-only, stale, unverified, ambiguous, unsuitable-scope, or materially contradicted support. The grade must be unknown.
